title: Pool Pulse: Rapid Triage & Preset Management for Dedicated GPU Capacity
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Platform customers running Redwood Dedicated need a single, scannable surface to triage GPU pool health, adjust autoscale parameters, and apply burst presets quickly during traffic anomalies. Current console flows scatter signals (metrics, logs, runbook links, burst controls) across multiple pages, causing delay during incidents and slow routine operations.

Goals:
- Surface a single 'Pool Pulse' strip that summarizes health (capacity headroom, queue depth, error rate, median latency) and links to deeper traces.
- Provide rapid, reversible controls: temporary burst presets (1-24h), safe autoscale tuning with guardrails, and one-click rollback.
- Make cost impact visible inline (estimated additional GPU-hours, estimated token cost uplift).
- Support runbook-driven triage actions (open incident, attach snapshot, escalate).

Users: SREs, platform engineers, and ops-focused product engineers managing Dedicated GPU pools for customers.

Proposed solution:
- Top-level compact card: Pool Pulse header with colored health state (OK/Degraded/Critical), time-to-slo, and quick actions (Burst, Scale, Snapshot, Runbook).
- Health timeline: condensed sparkline band showing CPU/GPU utilization, queue length, 95/99 latency, and error spikes; hover reveals exact points.
- Autoscale preview: mini-curve editor allowing operator to nudge min/max or change target utilization with immediate preview of expected throughput and cost delta.
- Burst presets panel: curated presets (Boost-Short, Boost-Extended, Emergency-Drain) and freeform duration slider with safety checks (permission, burst budget). Applying a preset opens a confirmation modal showing projected cost and auto-revert time.
- Triage drawer: attaches recent logs, recent model routes impacted, active requests table, and link to the rollout that may be correlated. From the drawer, operators can attach snapshot artifacts to an incident ticket.
- Accessibility: keyboard-first controls for critical actions, ARIA live regions for state changes, and color contrast tuned to WCAG AA for status badges.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Avoid overwhelming the card with raw metrics; prioritize signal-to-noise and link to full dashboards for deep dives.
- Cost estimates are modeled from heuristics and flagged as "estimated"; exact billing lives in billing console.
- Autoscale changes use staged rollout by default (canary window) unless the operator explicitly chooses immediate apply.

Acceptance criteria: see separate field.

Prototype & artifacts: link to Figma prototype and design spec provided below.

Success metrics: reduction in mean time to triage for pool incidents by 30% and decreased frequency of emergency manual scale-ups because presets are available and trusted.

acceptance_criteria: A compact Pool Pulse card renders in the Dedicated Pool overview for pools with dedicated capacity.
Health badge accurately reflects computed health state derived from metrics (utilization, queue, latency, error rate).
Applying a burst preset opens a confirmation modal that shows estimated cost, duration, and auto-revert time; applying creates an audit event.
Autoscale editor can propose a change and preview expected throughput and estimated cost delta without committing changes.
Operators can open a triage drawer from the card that includes recent logs snapshot, active request list, and runbook link.
All interactive controls meet keyboard accessibility and ARIA recommendations per design doc.
next_steps: Design handoff: export tokens, motion specs, and annotated frames for ENG-44210 (due 2026-03-14).
Work with Eng (Samir) to confirm telemetry field names and rate limits; ensure mock data for e2e QA.
PM to add feature flag and billing estimate hook (PM-221).
Schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with SRE rotation (2026-03-16) and collect prioritization feedback.
Prepare a short demo script for the March customer partner review.
accessibility_considerations: Keyboard-first interaction for all critical actions; ARIA live regions announcing state changes (e.g., 'Burst applied for 1 hour, estimated cost $X'); contrast and focus states validated to WCAG AA; all modals trap focus and return focus to invoking element on close.
notes_for_engineering: Include feature-flag gate, audit logging for burst and autoscale changes, and include a dry-run API for autoscale preview. Autoscale changes should default to staged canary unless the operator selects immediate apply. See ENG-44999 for telemetry fields and ENG-44210 for implementation owner.
